summary: This program stores a car's attributes in a single tuple and then reads values back out by their position. It shows that a tuple groups related values in a fixed order that cannot be changed after it is created.

lines.text: The parentheses open a tuple, an ordered collection whose contents are locked once created. Spreading it over several lines keeps each attribute readable.
The first value sits at index 0, so position alone tells you what this item means. The comment is the only label a tuple gives you, which is its main weakness compared with a dictionary.
A tuple can mix types freely: strings, integers, and floats all live side by side here.
The last item needs no trailing comma, and the closing parenthesis on the next line ends the tuple.
Square brackets pull out items by index, counting from zero, so car[0] is the make and car[2] is the year.
Indexes can be used in any order, but you have to remember which number holds which attribute — the reason a real program would prefer named fields.
